newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stockholm bourse hits record high at close.
newsitem.headline: Stockholm bourse hits record high at close.

text.p: The Stockholm bourse closed at a record high on Friday on underlying strength, not without some market anxiety that the rollercoaster ride resembled that of the late 1980's.
The Stockholm bourse general index closed 1.52 percent higher at 2,256.80, a record high after 2,223.16 on November 15.
"It doesn't feel as it it is going to flag," one broker tolod Reuters. It's a case of 'ride the bullet' - grab what is going well like banks and finance companies, drop what cannot keep up."
"As weak as it was on the bourse in 1992 before the crown was floated, that's as strong as it is today," said one dealer.

"It seems as if people have lost sight of fundamentals and and going with the flow. It is a bit like the 1980's and you really have to wonder if it is order-driven. There's a lot of market trading and everyone taking positions is long."
Banks were again in focus ahead of the weekend, amid fresh rumours of a restructuring.
S-E-Banken rose one to 62 crowns and Handelsbanken was up eight at 187.
Hennes & Mauritz again probed 1,000 crowns and hit 999 in intraday trading but closed at 987.
Heavyweights including Astra were behind the main index rise but Pharmacia & Upjohn eased against the trend 3.50 to 247.50.
Astra buoyed by overnight gains in the U.S. put on 4.50 to 317.50. Ericsson announced it would restructure into three business divisions and rose 3.50 to 204.50.
Volvo made a late rally to close the day 5.50 higher at 144.
